summary.text: Brown is the Democratic nominee and a former three-term U.S. senator from Ohio (2007-2025) who lost re-election to Bernie Moreno in 2024. A native of Mansfield, he began in the Ohio House at age 22, then served as secretary of state (1983-1991) and in the U.S. House (1993-2007) before winning the Senate seat in 2006. He is running to win back a seat for Democrats in the 2026 special election.

paragraphs.text: Born November 9, 1952, in Mansfield, Ohio, the son of Emily and Dr. Charles Gailey Brown.
Earned a bachelor's degree in Russian studies from Yale University in 1974, and later earned master's degrees in education and in public administration from Ohio State University.
Taught at Ohio State University's Mansfield campus from 1979 to 1981.
Elected to the Ohio House of Representatives while still in college and served as a state representative from 1975 to 1982; at his election, he was the youngest person elected to that body.
Elected Ohio Secretary of State in 1982 and re-elected in 1986, serving from 1983 to 1991; he lost a 1990 re-election bid to Republican Bob Taft.
Won the open seat for Ohio's 13th Congressional District in 1992 and served in the U.S. House from 1993 to 2007.

Elected to the U.S. Senate in 2006, defeating incumbent Mike DeWine, and re-elected in 2012 and 2018. He was the ranking Democrat on the Banking Committee from 2015 and chaired the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs from 2021 to 2025; he also served on the Finance, Agriculture, and Veterans' Affairs committees.

Lost re-election to Bernie Moreno in 2024, 50.1% to 46.5%. After leaving office he was a Spring 2025 visiting fellow at the Harvard Kennedy School and launched the Dignity of Work Institute, and on August 18, 2025, announced his candidacy for the 2026 special election.
